description.summary: the compositor types a stored secret for the secrets daemon

protocol.description:
The CrownOS secrets daemon (crownos-secretsd) keeps passwords and API keys that AI agents may use by name without ever reading the value. When an agent asks to type a secret into a field, the daemon hands the value to the compositor through this protocol, and the compositor types it. The value never passes through the agent, the accessibility bus or the clipboard.
Only crownos-secretsd may bind the manager global: the compositor checks the executable behind the client when it connects (exe:/usr/bin/crownos-secretsd, owned by root and checked by device and inode) and must not advertise the global to any other client. The daemon connects before it turns off PR_SET_DUMPABLE, so the compositor can read who it is. The daemon takes typing requests only from the installed computer-use daemon (exe:/usr/bin/crownos-computer-use, owned by root), which proves the focus in the browser before it asks.
Before a secret is used for a run template or an HTTPS proxy session, the daemon asks the user through ask_consent too. The compositor shows that question in the same consent dialog, so no D-Bus service or user service is in the path of a consent.
The compositor's own confirmation is mandatory and is the only confirmation for typing. For each committed request the compositor must:
- check that the window exists (else unknown_window) and that the verified app key of the client that owns it is the expected_app_key of the request (else target_mismatch). The app key is the one the compositor read when the client connected (sandbox:, exe: or interp:); the app_id that a toplevel sets for itself is never trusted; - refuse while the session is locked (session_locked), and refuse a terminal emulator, known by its app id, its app key or by a text_input_v3 content purpose of terminal (refused): text typed there is a command line; - show one confirmation for the whole request that names the agent, every secret name, the verified app (its name and executable), the window title, and the origin. The compositor draws the confirmation itself, or starts the root-owned consent dialog itself and takes an allow only when that same process mapped its dialog surface and exited with allow; synthetic input (crownos_input, virtual keyboards, agent cursors, driven seats) never reaches it, and no D-Bus service is in the path. The agent and origin strings are display text only: the compositor names the agent as coming "via crownos-secretsd". No answer within 120 seconds is timed_out; a deny is cancelled; - after an allow, check that the window still has the title that the confirmation showed (else focus_changed); - after an allow, check that the keyboard focus is on a surface of the window (else focus_changed) and, when require_password_field is set, that the focused text_input_v3 has the content purpose password before each value of kind password (else not_password_field). A client without an active text_input_v3 gets not_password_field when a password field is required, and refused otherwise: the check fails closed; - flag the window sensitive before the first key and keep the flag for 30 seconds after the last one, so screenshots, screencasts and the context engine do not see the field while it fills; - type each value in order through the text_input_v3 commit_string of the focused client, and press Tab on the user's seat after a value that asks for it. It types nothing that is not in a value; - zero its copies of the values and close the fds as soon as the request ends, and never log a value or send it to any other client.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Requests made through it are unaffected.

request.name: create_request

description.summary: start a typing request for one window

request.description: Starts a request for the window with this ext_foreign_toplevel identifier. Add one or more values, then commit. agent, secret_name and origin are display text for the confirmation; origin is empty when there is none and is a hint only.

arg.name: expected_app_key
arg.summary: the app key the daemon expects the window's client to have

arg.name: require_password_field
arg.summary: 1 to type only into a password field

arg.name: secret_name
arg.summary: the secret names, display text only

arg.name: origin
arg.summary: the page origin, display text only, or empty

request.name: ask_consent

description.summary: ask the user before a secret is used for a run or a proxy

request.description: crownos-secretsd asks the user whether an agent may use secrets for a registered run template or an HTTPS proxy session. The compositor shows the same consent dialog it shows for typing, bound to this request, and answers once with consent. agent_app_key, secret_names and detail are display text only: the compositor names the agent as coming "via crownos-secretsd". No answer within 120 seconds, a closed dialog, or a dialog that did not show itself is granted 0. Destroying the object withdraws the question and closes the dialog.

arg.name: agent_app_key
arg.summary: the agent's app key, display text only

arg.name: secret_names
arg.summary: the secret names, display text only

arg.name: detail
arg.summary: the template or the proxy hosts, display text only

interface.name: crownos_secret_input_request_v1

description.summary: one confirmed typing of one or more values

interface.description: Destroying the object before done cancels the request; the compositor then types nothing more.

entry.name: username
entry.summary: a user name or other visible text

entry.name: focus_changed
entry.summary: the focus was not on the window

entry.name: not_password_field
entry.summary: the focused field is not a password field

entry.name: refused
entry.summary: a bad value, a terminal, or another refusal

entry.name: cancelled
entry.summary: the user said no, or the request was destroyed

entry.name: timed_out
entry.summary: nobody answered the confirmation in time

entry.name: target_mismatch
entry.summary: the window's client does not have the expected app key

request.name: destroy
request.description: Cancels a request that has not sent done.

request.name: add_value
request.description: The fd must be a memfd sealed with F_SEAL_WRITE, F_SEAL_SHRINK and F_SEAL_GROW, holding UTF-8 text of at most 4096 bytes without control characters. Anything else makes the request end with done(refused) at commit; it is not a protocol error. The compositor reads the value once, closes the fd, and zeroes its copy after use.

arg.name: tab_after
arg.summary: 1 to press Tab after this value

request.name: commit
request.description: Starts the checks, the confirmation and the typing. done follows.

event.name: done
event.description: Sent once. The object does nothing more afterwards; destroy it.

interface.name: crownos_secret_consent_v1

description.summary: one consent question for a run or a proxy

interface.description: Destroying the object before consent withdraws the question.

entry.name: run
entry.summary: run a registered template with secrets in its environment

entry.name: proxy
entry.summary: add secrets to HTTPS requests through a proxy

request.name: destroy
request.description: Withdraws a question that has not had its answer.

event.name: consent
event.description: Sent once. 1 when the user allowed, 0 otherwise.
